What the differences mean

  • Panel size: 6 W ÷ 2.2 W = 2.7 times the eufy S340's panel rating. 6 W ÷ 2.5 W = 2.4 times the Tapo C660's charging limit. A bigger panel refills the battery faster on short or cloudy days.
  • Daily drain at the same rating: eufy and Reolink both rate battery life at 300 seconds of recording a day. That gives 10,000 mAh ÷ about 90 days ≈ 111 mAh a day for the S340 and 5,000 mAh ÷ about 60 days ≈ 83 mAh a day for the Argus 4 Pro. On those ratings, the S340's larger battery lasts about 30 more days with no sun.
  • Tapo's sun claim: TP-Link says 45 minutes of sun runs the C660 for a day at up to 100 events. 2.5 W × 0.75 h ≈ 1.9 Wh a day at most, measured at 1,000 W/m² and 77 °F (25 °C).
  • Argus Eco Ultra: 21.6 Wh ÷ 120 days ≈ 0.18 Wh a day, using Reolink's 4-month best case, which gives no recording basis.

Why a solar camera stops charging below 32 °F

Lithium batteries can't safely take a charge below freezing, so each maker blocks charging there, however bright the sun. Reolink's support page gives a 0–45 °C (32–113 °F) charging range for its Solar Panel, Solar Panel 2 and Solar Panel 3, and says 'charging may temporarily stop when the current temperature is below 0°C to protect the lithium battery.' eufy's SoloCam S340 manual gives a charging range of 0–40 °C (32–104 °F), even though the camera is rated to operate down to -4 °F. Tapo lists 32–113 °F for the C660 KIT, and its 45-minutes-of-sun claim is measured at 77 °F. On a clear 20 °F week, none of these panels adds any charge, and the camera runs on its own battery.

Reolink's Solar Panel 2S is the one workaround in this group. It has its own 5,900 mAh (42.48 Wh) battery. Between 0 °C and -20 °C (32 °F to -4 °F), that battery powers the camera directly instead of charging it, so the camera's battery level holds. The 2S recharges its own battery from 14 °F (-10 °C) and stops powering the camera below -4 °F. Reolink lists every battery camera as compatible except the original Argus, the Keen and the Reolink Doorbell (Battery), and names the Argus 4 Pro.

Long-term evidence: Notebookcheck's Benedikt Winkel ran an Argus 4 Pro on solar for six months. It lost power only once, when snow covered the panel for several days. Techtest.org measured about one month on battery alone for the Tapo C660, and expects a few manual recharges in winter.

Not recommended

The eufy SoloCam S340 at full price. eufy's US store charges $219.99 for it. For $229.99, the same store sells the SoloCam E50, which eufy bills as the 'S340 Next-Gen': two 4K lenses, a 5 W solar panel with MPPT charging, and dual-band Wi-Fi, where the S340 has a 2.2 W panel and 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only. Buy the S340 only at a clear discount.
